outcome: No proof of the volume conjecture for all knots has appeared since 26 January 2024, and Wikipedia's lead (last edited 19 November 2025) still calls it open; the window instead holds unrefereed or partial claims for infinite families of knots (twist knots, double twist knots), cone-angle and complex-parameter results for the figure-eight knot, computer-assisted results for a neighbouring Andersen-Kashaev form, and a September 2026 Chen-Yang (Turaev-Viro) 3-manifold preprint whose acknowledgement names an AI model that I could not verify.
problem_asks: (a) For a knot K in S^3, a quantum invariant of K: the colored Jones polynomial J_N(K; q), in the standard Kashaev/Murakami form evaluated at q = exp(2 pi i / N) (the Kashaev invariant <K>_N, normalised). (b) The exponential growth rate of that invariant as N tends to infinity. (c) That growth rate is determined by hyperbolic geometry of the knot complement S^3 minus K: in the standard form, lim_{N->inf} (2 pi / N) log|<K>_N| = Vol(S^3 minus K), the simplicial volume, which for a hyperbolic knot is its hyperbolic volume. (d) The frozen wording is loose: it does not fix the root of unity, the normalisation, or the volume (hyperbolic versus simplicial), and it says 'quantum invariants' without naming one. The record takes the Murakami-Murakami simplicial form (as in the Wikipedia lead) as the working statement and treats other quantum invariants (Teichmuller TQFT / Andersen-Kashaev, Turaev-Viro for 3-manifolds, quantum modular forms) as neighbouring formulations. The statement quantifies over all knots, so a result for one family settles only that family.

events.what_happened: R. M. Kashaev and O. Tirkkonen posted 'Proof of the volume conjecture for torus knots' (arXiv math/9912210). The abstract says the volume conjecture, 'formulated recently by H. Murakami and J. Murakami, is proved for the case of torus knots'. The abstract does not name the invariant. Wikipedia lists torus knots as a verified case.
events.delivers: Volume conjecture for torus knots. These are not hyperbolic; their complements are Seifert fibred, so the volume term is zero and the limit is zero. Covers one zero-volume class of knots.
events.remains: All hyperbolic knots, and the general knot statement.
events.doubts: Journal status not checked. The abstract is the only statement of scope I read; the 5-page paper was not read.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture, in the zero-volume case.

events.what_happened: Proof of the volume conjecture for the figure-eight knot 4_1, credited to Tobias Ekholm (Wikipedia's list of verified cases). The primary paper was not located. A search summary of a Murakami survey and of Murakami's 2000 paper on colored Jones asymptotics says the limit of log(J_N(4_1))/N was calculated by Ekholm and confirms Kashaev's conjecture for 4_1. I did not open those sources.
events.delivers: Full volume conjecture for the figure-eight knot, a hyperbolic knot.
events.remains: All other hyperbolic knots.
events.doubts: Date is only a year bound, from an unopened source. Primary paper not located.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture for 4_1.

events.what_happened: Yoshiyuki Yokota, 'On the volume conjecture for hyperbolic knots' (arXiv math/0009165, 18 Sep 2000). An informal argument for Kashaev's conjecture for hyperbolic knots, in which hyperbolicity equations from diagrams correspond to stationary-phase equations for Kashaev's invariants. The author calls it 'a rough, and so not complete yet, proof'.
events.delivers: Heuristic argument for the hyperbolic-knot conjecture, self-described as incomplete.
events.remains: Everything: no complete proof is claimed.
events.doubts: The author's own statement that the proof is incomplete.
events.direction: Supports the conjecture heuristically; not a proof.

events.what_happened: Stavros Garoufalidis and Thang T. Q. Le, 'Asymptotics of the colored Jones function of a knot' (arXiv math/0508100, first submitted 4 Aug 2005; v6 revised 31 Aug 2011). The abstract opened does not mention the Borromean rings. A search snippet reports an appendix, 'The volume conjecture for the Borromean rings' (Theorem A.1), which I did not read in full. A search summary gives publication in Geometry & Topology 15 (2011). Wikipedia lists the Borromean rings as a verified case.
events.delivers: Volume conjecture for the Borromean rings, a three-component hyperbolic link (complement volume 2 v_8, from two regular ideal octahedra, per the snippet). This is a link, not a knot.
events.remains: All knots, and the knot statement. Whether links fall under this problem's wording is a scope question.

checked_by.qualification: Refereed journal; publication reported in a search summary, not confirmed on the journal page by me

events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture for a hyperbolic link.

events.what_happened: Hao Zheng, arXiv math/0508138 (August 2005): volume conjecture for Whitehead doubles of a family of torus knots. The v1 title and abstract refer to Whitehead doubles of torus knots in general; later versions say 'a family'. A search summary gives publication in Chinese Annals of Mathematics, Series B, 28(4), 2007. Wikipedia lists the case as Whitehead doubles of T(p,q) with q = 2, crediting Zheng.
events.revisions: v1 Aug 2005; later versions changed the scope wording (per search summary).
events.delivers: Volume conjecture for Whitehead doubles of a family of torus knots (Wikipedia: q = 2). The companion is a torus knot, so the complement's volume comes from the Whitehead link complement.
events.remains: Whitehead doubles outside the family, and all hyperbolic knots.

checked_by.who: Chinese Annals of Mathematics, Series B (journal)
checked_by.qualification: Refereed journal; publication reported in a search result, not opened by me

events.doubts: The scope wording differs between versions, so the exact family is not settled from the abstract. I did not open the arXiv paper.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture for the stated family.

events.what_happened: Roland van der Veen, 'A cabling formula for the colored Jones polynomial' (arXiv 0807.2679, first submitted 17 Jul 2008). The paper proves an explicit cabling formula; as an application it proves the volume conjecture for all zero-volume knots and links, those obtained from the unknot by repeated cabling and connected sum. The abstract opened states this as proved with no stated hypotheses.
events.delivers: Volume conjecture for all zero-volume knots and links built from the unknot by cabling and connected sum. None is hyperbolic.
events.remains: All hyperbolic knots.
events.doubts: Journal status not checked. The full argument was not read.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture in the zero-volume case.

events.what_happened: Roland van der Veen, 'Proof of the volume conjecture for Whitehead chains' (arXiv math/0611181, Nov 2006; search summary says published in Acta Mathematica Vietnamica, 2008). Per a search snippet, the paper treats an infinite family of non-split links generalising the Whitehead link and the Borromean rings. It reports that the naive limit fails for even colours (J_N vanishes at a root of unity for even N) but holds for odd colours, and that the original conjecture may fail for non-split links; it proposes a limsup version for links. I did not open this paper.
events.revisions: A later version is referred to in the snippet as stating the failure for non-split links.
events.delivers: Links only: a volume statement for Whitehead chains, with odd colours, and a limsup modification for links. Says the original form fails for some non-split links.
events.remains: Knots are untouched by this paper.
events.doubts: Based on a snippet only. The claim that the original form may fail for links is the one bearing on Wikipedia's statement that the conjecture is known to be false for arbitrary links.
events.direction: For links, the all-colour limit is said to fail in some cases; this is a claim about links, not knots.

events.what_happened: Thang T. Q. Le and Anh T. Tran, 'On the volume conjecture for cables of knots' (arXiv 0907.0172, first submitted 1 Jul 2009; v3 20 Aug 2009). Abstract opened: they prove the volume conjecture for (m,2)-cables of the figure-eight knot when m is odd. For (m,2)-cables of general knots with m even, the limit depends on the parity of the colour. For many cables of the figure-eight knot the volume conjecture fails if all colours are considered but holds when colours are restricted to a subset.
events.delivers: Volume conjecture for (m,2)-cables of 4_1 with m odd. Cable complements are not hyperbolic; the volume term is the figure-eight complement's. Also records a failure of the all-colour form for some cables.
events.remains: Cables with m even, cables of other knots, and all hyperbolic knots.
events.doubts: Journal status not checked.
events.direction: Consistent for odd m. The all-colour failure is a failure of one formulation for those cables, not a counterexample to the conjecture for knots in general.

events.what_happened: Fathi Ben Aribi, Francois Gueritaud and Eiichi Piguet-Nakazawa, 'Geometric triangulations and the Teichmuller TQFT volume conjecture for twist knots' (arXiv 1903.09480, first submitted 22 Mar 2019; v5 24 Jun 2022). Abstract: they build an infinite family of geometric triangulations of twist-knot complements, compute the Teichmuller TQFT partition function, and use the saddle-point method to prove the volume conjecture for all twist knots. The companion short note (Comptes Rendus Math. 357 (2019) 299-305, per search result) first announced the result for 'all twist knots up to 14 crossings'. The v5 comment says it was accepted in Quantum Topology; a search summary gives Quantum Topology 14 (2023), 285-406, DOI 10.4171/QT/178.
events.delivers: Volume conjecture in the Teichmuller TQFT (Andersen-Kashaev) form for all twist knots, stated without conditional hypotheses in the abstract. This is a different formulation from the Kashaev invariant at roots of unity.
events.remains: The Kashaev / colored Jones form for twist knots (not addressed in this paper); all other knots.

checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted for publication per the v5 comment; published per a search summary

events.doubts: Scope changed between the 2019 note ('up to 14 crossings', per search result) and the paper ('all twist knots', abstract opened).
events.direction: Consistent with the Andersen-Kashaev form of the conjecture for twist knots.

events.what_happened: Qingtao Chen and Shengmao Zhu, two arXiv papers on asymptotic expansions of the colored Jones polynomial of twist knots K_p (p >= 6). Part I (arXiv 2307.12963, first submitted 24 Jul 2023; v2 revised 13 Jun 2025) at the root e^{2 pi i/(N+1/2)}. Part II (arXiv 2307.13670, 25 Jul 2023) at e^{2 pi i/(N+1/M)} with M >= 2, and by letting M tend to infinity at e^{2 pi i/N}, the KMM root. Both abstracts state an asymptotic expansion formula. Neither abstract states that the volume conjecture is proved for twist knots.
events.revisions: Part I: v1 24 Jul 2023; v2 13 Jun 2025 (content of the revision not checked). Part II: v1 25 Jul 2023 only.
events.delivers: Asymptotic expansions of the colored Jones polynomial of twist knots at the KMM root (Part II, by limit). Does not by itself state the growth-rate-equals-volume limit.
events.remains: The volume statement itself, which would require a growth estimate from these expansions; all knots outside twist knots.
events.doubts: A search summary attributes to Ge-Meng-Wang-Yang (2024) a statement that Chen and Zhu 'asserted' the KMM conjecture for twist knots with p' >= 6. I could not confirm that: the Ge et al. abstract page I opened does not mention Chen or Zhu. Unresolved.
events.direction: Expansions consistent with the conjecture; no volume limit stated in the abstract.

events.what_happened: Sukuse Abe, 'Proof of Volume Conjecture for twist knots' (arXiv 2012.05441, single author). The abstract (latest version) says: 'We prove the volume conjecture for any twist knots by using an equivalence relation, complex analysis, analytic continuation, and function of several complex variables on the basis of colored Jones polynomials.' Nineteen versions. A search summary says earlier versions described the method differently, one naming steepest descent. The author's own conference abstract (10th WorldS4, listed for 30 Jul 2026, not opened) repeats the claim.
events.delivers: Claims the volume conjecture for any twist knot, with the form of the claim (colour sequence, form of limit) not stated in the abstract. Abstract-level claim only; the argument was not read.
events.remains: Double twist knots beyond twist knots (see Jun Murakami 2024/25), and all other knots.
events.time_since_posted: 5 years 10 months since v1; 2 years 4 months since last revision
events.doubts: (1) No journal publication found. (2) Nineteen versions over about 3.5 years, with the method described differently across versions (search summary). (3) No referee report, published comment, erratum or withdrawal found in the searches I ran; those searches are not exhaustive (no MathSciNet, zbMATH or MathOverflow search). (4) The abstract's method is terse; the full argument was not read. (5) Overlaps with the 2023-25 Chen-Zhu claim for the same family, which is not established.
events.direction: Claims the conjecture for an infinite family of hyperbolic knots, with the classical colored-Jones form.

events.what_happened: Renaud Detcherry, Efstratia Kalfagianni and Tian Yang, 'Turaev-Viro invariants, colored Jones polynomials and volume' (arXiv 1701.07818, first submitted 26 Jan 2017; Quantum Topology 2018 per search summary). They express Turaev-Viro invariants of link complements via colored Jones values, test the Chen-Yang volume conjecture, verify it for the figure-eight knot and Borromean rings, and report asymptotic behaviour of colored Jones values 'that seem not to be predicted by neither the Kashaev-Murakami-Murakami volume conjecture nor by Zagier's quantum modularity conjecture'.
events.delivers: Turaev-Viro (3-manifold) form of the volume conjecture for figure-eight and Borromean rings complements. Not the colored Jones growth limit of the KMM form.
events.remains: The KMM / colored Jones limit for knots.

checked_by.qualification: Refereed journal; publication reported in a search summary

events.direction: Turaev-Viro form consistent for two hyperbolic complements. The authors state the colored Jones asymptotics show phenomena the KMM form does not predict, a scope note for this problem.

events.what_happened: Ka Ho Wong, arXiv 1912.11779 (Dec 2019): for links whose complements split into several hyperbolic pieces, colored Jones polynomials at the (N+1/2)-th root of unity; growth rates recover simplicial volume; proves the Turaev-Viro volume conjecture for these links and proposes a generalisation using incomplete hyperbolic structures (search snippet; not opened).
events.delivers: Links with several hyperbolic pieces, at the half-integer root; a link result in the colored Jones form.
events.remains: Knots in the knot statement, and single-piece hyperbolic links.
events.doubts: Based on a snippet only.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture for these links, at a different root of unity.

events.what_happened: Stavros Garoufalidis and Seokbeom Yoon, '1-loop equals torsion for two-bridge knots' (arXiv 2411.03801, v1 6 Nov 2024; v2 13 Nov 2024). Motivated by the conjectured asymptotics of the Kashaev invariant; proves that the constant (1-loop) term of the Dimofte-Garoufalidis power series equals the adjoint Reidemeister torsion for hyperbolic 2-bridge knots, combining work of Ohtsuki and Takata.
events.delivers: The constant term of the asymptotic expansion, for hyperbolic 2-bridge knots, equals adjoint torsion. Says nothing about the exponential growth rate.
events.remains: The growth-rate-equals-volume statement, for all knots.
events.doubts: The abstract says the proof uses 'an explicit computation' without saying how; I did not read the body.
events.direction: Neighbouring: refines the asymptotic expansion, does not move the volume limit.

events.what_happened: Fathi Ben Aribi and Ka Ho Wong, 'The Andersen-Kashaev volume conjecture for FAMED geometric triangulations' (arXiv 2410.10776, v1 14 Oct 2024; v2 27 Feb 2026). Abstract (paraphrased by the fetch tool; the claims are quoted in part): for FAMED triangulations of one-cusped hyperbolic 3-manifolds with trivial second homology, the Jones function exists in Teichmuller TQFT and an asymptotic expansion gives the Andersen-Kashaev volume conjecture; the results cover every hyperbolic twist knot and the first 42,000 hyperbolic knots in S^3.
events.delivers: Andersen-Kashaev (Teichmuller TQFT state-integral) volume conjecture for every hyperbolic twist knot, and for the FAMED-triangulated knots among the first 42,000 hyperbolic knots in S^3. Restricted to FAMED triangulations. Not the Kashaev / colored Jones form.
events.remains: The Kashaev / colored Jones form; all knots not covered by the FAMED condition.
events.doubts: Whether the Andersen-Kashaev form is the same problem as the Kashaev-Murakami-Murakami form is a scope call; the abstract does not say they are equivalent. The 42,000-knot count is a computer-search result (see next event).
events.direction: Consistent with the Andersen-Kashaev conjecture for the stated cases.

events.what_happened: Huabin Ge, Yunpeng Meng, Chuwen Wang and Yuxuan Yang, 'On the Volume Conjecture for hyperbolic Dehn-filled 3-manifolds along the twist knots' (arXiv 2410.20489, 27 Oct 2024, single version). Proves the Chen-Yang volume conjecture for closed 3-manifolds obtained by (p,q) Dehn filling of twist-knot complements when |p|+|q| and |p'| are large, using a new ideal triangulation of the Whitehead link complement.
events.delivers: Turaev-Viro / Chen-Yang form for large Dehn fillings of twist-knot complements. A 3-manifold result, not the colored Jones growth statement for knot complements.
events.remains: The Kashaev / colored Jones form, and all knot complements in S^3.
events.doubts: Does not mention the KMM form or Chen-Zhu / Abe in the abstract page I read. The search summary's claim that Ge et al. say Chen and Zhu asserted the KMM conjecture for twist knots is unconfirmed.
events.direction: Consistent with the Chen-Yang form for the stated fillings.

events.what_happened: Jun Murakami, 'Complexified tetrahedrons, fundamental groups, and volume conjecture for double twist knots' (arXiv 2501.00225). v1 31 Dec 2024; v2 4 Mar 2025 (per the fetch); v3 2 May 2025, with comment 'add Appendix E, fix the gap of Lemma B'. Abstract: proves the volume conjecture for double twist knots, using complexified tetrahedra and an SL(2,C) representation of the fundamental group; colored Jones polynomial written via a quantum 6j symbol. Talks in 2024 (Tokyo seminar listing, Kyoto slides) preceded the arXiv posting; the write-up date is used here.
events.revisions: v1 31 Dec 2024; v2 4 Mar 2025; v3 2 May 2025 (adds Appendix E, fixes a gap in Lemma B).
events.delivers: Claims the volume conjecture for all double twist knots. The abstract does not say which form (colored Jones at e^{2 pi i/N} or complexified SL(2,C)) is proved. The 2024 slides state the target as 2 pi lim log|V_{N-1}(K)|/N = Vol + i CS, the complexified form. A seminar abstract says the ADO invariant is used in place of colored Jones. Both points need checking.
events.remains: Whether the claim is the Kashaev/colored Jones form; all knots outside double twist knots.
events.doubts: (1) The author himself records a gap in Lemma B, repaired in v3; the repair is not independently checked. (2) The seminar abstract says the ADO invariant replaces colored Jones, which would change the object. (3) Target statement is the complexified form, so the real part needs checking against the Wikipedia form. (4) No journal publication found. (5) No external engagement found in searches; these are not exhaustive. (6) Double twist knots include twist knots, so this overlaps the Abe claim.
events.direction: Claims the conjecture for an infinite family of hyperbolic knots, in a complexified SL(2,C) form that may differ from the colored Jones form.

events.what_happened: Mark Hughes, Vishnu Jejjala, P. Ramadevi, Pratik Roy and Vivek Kumar Singh, 'Colored Jones Polynomials and the Volume Conjecture' (arXiv 2502.18575, v1 25 Feb 2025; cross-listed cs.LG). They compute spin-1 (adjoint, 3-coloured) Jones polynomials for hyperbolic knots up to 15 crossings; a fully connected feedforward network trained on part of the data predicts knot-complement volume from the adjoint polynomial with 99.34% accuracy; a single evaluation at q = e^{8 pi i/15} predicts volume almost as well; from 2- and 3-coloured data they conjecture the best phase for n-coloured polynomials, and propose an improved statement of the volume conjecture with phase q(n) = exp(2 pi i (n+1)/(n(n+2))), tested on the figure-eight knot and K_0 at finite n (per the HTML fetch). A Cambridge talk (June 2025) presented the same material.
events.revisions: v1 25 Feb 2025 only, per the abstract page.
events.delivers: Numerical evidence and a modified conjecture with a different phase. It proves no case of the original statement. The authors present the volume conjecture as open, and the improved version as a hypothesis.
events.remains: The original volume conjecture for all knots, unchanged.
events.doubts: Numerical and data-driven; the improved statement is a changed version, not a result on the problem as stated. The HTML fetch says the authors report slow, non-monotonic convergence for one 18-crossing knot. Journal status not found.
events.direction: Proposes a different phase and an improved (changed) statement; supports the volume connection numerically.

systems.name: fully connected feedforward neural network
systems.what_it_did: Trained on a subset of the adjoint-Jones dataset (75/10/15 split; five hidden layers, per the HTML fetch) to predict hyperbolic knot-complement volume from the adjoint Jones polynomial or its evaluations, with 99.34% accuracy. It is a machine-learning tool the authors built, not a named AI product. The phase conjecture is drawn from the analysis of 2- and 3-coloured polynomials; the network's accuracy motivated but did not prove it. Code is on GitHub (ColoredJonesML); authorship of the code is not stated.
systems.basis_quote: The abstract, as rendered by the fetch tool (wording not verbatim): the authors 'conjecture the best phase for n-colored Jones polynomials' and 'use this hypothesis to motivate an improved statement of the volume conjecture'.

events.what_happened: Shengmao Zhu gave a seminar at the ShanghaiTech Institute of Mathematical Sciences (listing dated 2025/0523; talk 29 May 2025 per a search summary) on joint work with Qingtao Chen. Per the listing abstract (search result, not opened), asymptotic expansions of the colored Jones polynomial of twist knots lead, 'as a consequence', to a proof of the volume conjecture for twist knots.
events.delivers: Claimed volume conjecture for twist knots. No written argument for it was opened by me; the arXiv series abstracts state only expansions.
events.remains: All knots outside twist knots; and any written verification of the claim.
events.doubts: Talk abstract only; the written proof, if any, was not found. Conflicting attribution in a search summary (see the Chen-Zhu 2023 event).
events.direction: Claims the conjecture for twist knots.

events.what_happened: Renaud Detcherry, Efstratia Kalfagianni and Shashini Marasinghe, 'Seifert cobordisms and the Chen-Yang volume conjecture' (arXiv 2505.01546, 2 May 2025, single version). Shows that the Turaev-Viro volume conjecture is preserved when a Seifert-fibred 3-manifold is glued along a boundary torus; applications: the conjecture for all Seifert-fibred 3-manifolds with boundary and for large classes of graph 3-manifolds.
events.delivers: Turaev-Viro form for Seifert-fibred and some graph 3-manifolds with boundary. Not knot complements in S^3 in the colored Jones form.
events.remains: The Kashaev / colored Jones statement for hyperbolic knot complements.
events.direction: Neighbouring Turaev-Viro form; consistent with the Chen-Yang conjecture for the stated class.

events.what_happened: Christoph Aistleitner and Manuel Hauke, 'On the behavior of the colored Jones polynomial of the figure-eight knot under modular transformations' (arXiv 2510.02188, 2 Oct 2025). Proves Zagier's continuity conjecture for h(x) = log(J_{4_1,0}(e^{2 pi i x}) / J_{4_1,0}(e^{2 pi i/x})) at all irrationals, for the figure-eight knot's Sudler-product colored Jones values.
events.delivers: Quantum modularity (a modular-transformation continuity statement) for the figure-eight knot at rational-type roots of unity. Not a volume statement and not the growth-rate limit.
events.remains: The volume conjecture for any knot.
events.direction: Neighbouring result on the same colored Jones values; does not address the volume statement.

events.what_happened: Pavel Putrov and Ayush Singh, 'On Quantum Modularity for Geometric 3-Manifolds' (arXiv 2512.10768, v1 11 Dec 2025; v2 16 Mar 2026, minor changes). States a strong quantum modularity conjecture for WRT invariants of closed geometric 3-manifolds, with a distinguished SL(2,C) flat connection; proves it for Brieskorn homology spheres and some other examples.
events.delivers: Quantum modularity for closed geometric 3-manifolds in some examples (Brieskorn spheres). Does not mention the volume conjecture.
events.remains: The volume conjecture for knots.
events.direction: Neighbouring quantum-modularity conjecture; does not address the volume statement.

events.what_happened: Fathi Ben Aribi, Antonin Guilloux and Ka Ho Wong, 'FAMED by computer: proving the Andersen-Kashaev volume conjecture for 42,000 knots' (arXiv 2512.17437, 19 Dec 2025). A computer search with Regina and SnapPy finds FAMED geometric triangulations for more than 42,000 knot complements in S^3, including all knots with 12 or fewer crossings, and proves the Andersen-Kashaev conjecture for them. The authors say the search gives insights toward a general proof. The Guilloux companion page (search result, not opened) gives 42,136 complements with 6 exceptions.
events.delivers: Andersen-Kashaev volume conjecture for the listed knots (all up to 12 crossings, and others with FAMED triangulations). Finite explicit list; no general knot. Not the Kashaev / colored Jones form.
events.remains: All hyperbolic knots, and the Kashaev / colored Jones form.

machine_checked.system: Regina and SnapPy computer search (not a proof assistant; no Lean or Coq record)

events.directly_checkable: Each certified case is a FAMED triangulation of a named knot complement, checkable with SnapPy and Regina.
events.doubts: Counting differs between sources (more than 42,000 here; 42,136 with 6 exceptions on the companion page). Computer-based; the code was not read.
events.direction: Consistent with the Andersen-Kashaev conjecture for the listed knots.

events.what_happened: Hitoshi Murakami, 'The generalized volume conjecture for the figure-eight knot parametrized by a complex number with small imaginary part' (arXiv 2602.01049, 1 Feb 2026, single version; 84 pages). Studies the N-dimensional colored Jones polynomial of the figure-eight knot at exp(xi/N) with 0 < Im xi < pi/2. Two regimes: for large Re xi the growth is governed by the Chern-Simons invariant; for small Re xi it converges to the reciprocal of the Alexander polynomial at exp(xi).
events.delivers: Asymptotic results for the figure-eight knot at complex parameters with small imaginary part, in two regimes. Not the volume statement at the standard root (xi real), and not for other knots.
events.remains: The standard-root volume statement for the figure-eight knot is already known (see Ekholm); all other knots.
events.doubts: Only the abstract and metadata were read (84-page paper). The abstract does not claim a full volume-conjecture proof for the figure-eight knot in this range.
events.direction: Analogue: complex-parameter generalisation for one knot. Neither confirms nor refutes the volume statement.

events.what_happened: Shinichiro Kakuta, 'On the volume conjecture of the colored Jones invariants with arbitrary colors' (arXiv 2604.10472; v1 12 Apr 2026, v2 7 May 2026, v3 4 Sep 2026). Colour sequences deform the hyperbolic structure, limits relate to volumes of cone manifolds with singular set the link. Theorem 1.2: Murakami's Conjecture 1.1 (cone-manifold volume form, cited as [19, Conjecture 4]) holds for the figure-eight knot with cone angles 0 <= alpha < alpha_0 = 1.7647826174..., where alpha_0 is a supremum defined by an inequality evaluated by computation. Theorem 1.4 (per the HTML fetch): an analogous region for the Borromean rings, which is a link. Remark 1.6: numerical checks for larger cone angles.
events.delivers: A cone-angle deformation of the volume statement for the figure-eight knot, for cone angles below alpha_0 (about 1.765); the alpha = 0 case is the standard figure-eight statement. For the Borromean rings (a link), a region of cone angles. The abstract-level claim is conditional on that range.
events.remains: Cone angles at or above alpha_0; the standard volume statement for other knots; the Kashaev form for general knots.
events.doubts: alpha_0 is defined through an inequality checked numerically ('by a computation'), so part of the proof is computer-assisted. Remark 1.6 says numerical checks beyond the proved range. No journal or referee found. Paper's own status: preprint.
events.direction: Analogue (cone-angle deformation) for the figure-eight knot, proved on a range; partial for the Borromean link.

events.what_happened: Ce Shen, 'The Chen-Yang volume conjecture for long integral fillings of fundamental shadow links' (arXiv 2609.11839; v1 10 Sep 2026, v2 11 Sep 2026, v3 20 Sep 2026). Proves the Chen-Yang volume conjecture (SO(3) Turaev-Viro growth recovers hyperbolic volume) for all sufficiently long integral Dehn fillings of a fixed marked fundamental shadow-link exterior; also a full asymptotic expansion of the signed SO(3) WRT invariant with leading coefficient in terms of adjoint Reidemeister torsion. The comments field says that after v1, the author was told by Yunpeng Meng, Baojun Wu, Tian Yang and Yuxuan Yang that they had independently obtained the same results and were preparing an article. AI NOTE, UNVERIFIED: a search result quoted the acknowledgements as saying 'The results were obtained with assistance from GPT-6 Astra.' and 'The author has checked the results and takes full responsibility for the content of this paper.' I could not read the acknowledgements myself: the PDF returned binary only, the HTML text returned ended mid-Appendix C.3 before any acknowledgements, and papers.cool shows no acknowledgements.
events.delivers: For fixed shadow-link exteriors and all integral fillings beyond a threshold: SO(3) Turaev-Viro growth recovers the hyperbolic volume of each filled manifold along odd levels. This is for 3-manifolds obtained by filling links, not the colored Jones growth of knot complements in S^3.
events.remains: The Kashaev / colored Jones volume statement for knots; fillings below the threshold.
events.doubts: Preprint days old; no public engagement found. The AI attribution is a quote I could not verify against the paper text. The independent-result note in the comments is a priority or independence matter for the Chen-Yang family.
events.direction: Consistent with the Chen-Yang Turaev-Viro conjecture for these 3-manifolds; a neighbouring formulation, not the knot statement.

disputes.summary: Twist-knot case. Abe (2020, rev. 2024) claims the classical volume conjecture for all twist knots. Chen and Zhu (2023 series; 2025 talk) claim the same for twist knots, but their abstracts state only expansions. A search summary attributes to Ge et al. (2024) the statement that Chen and Zhu asserted it; I could not confirm that. Jun Murakami (2024-25) claims double twist knots, in a complexified form. Ben Aribi, Gueritaud and Piguet-Nakazawa (2019, QT 2023) prove the Teichmuller TQFT (Andersen-Kashaev) form for all twist knots. These are overlapping claims in different forms; none is a priority contest visible in the sources.
Chen-Yang family independence. The Shen preprint's comments say Meng, Wu, Yang and Yang independently obtained the same results and were preparing an article; no resolution is visible in the sources.

Zheng (2005): v1 says Whitehead doubles of torus knots in general; later versions say 'a family' of torus knots (search summary). Scope of the proved family is therefore not settled from the abstract.

summary: I ran 51 verbatim searches and opened the primary preprints for every in-window event, plus the Wikipedia article (last edited 19 Nov 2025; lists verified cases as figure-eight (Ekholm), three-twist knot, Borromean rings, torus knots, volume-zero knots and links, twisted Whitehead links, and Whitehead doubles of T(p,q) with q = 2; says the conjecture is open in general and known to be false for arbitrary links; cites nothing after 2010). Findings in the window: (1) No source I could find claims or shows the conjecture for all knots; no retraction, no disproof and no formal verification. (2) Claimed proofs for infinite families of knots, all unrefereed, with different forms: Jun Murakami (arXiv 2501.00225, first posted 31 Dec 2024; v3 May 2025 repairs a Lemma B gap that the author records) for double twist knots in a complexified SL(2,C) form; Abe (arXiv 2012.05441, first posted 10 Dec 2020, last revised 1 Jun 2024, 19 versions) for all twist knots in the classical form, which is pre-window but still live in revisions; and a Chen-Zhu talk claim (May 2025) for twist knots, whose written proof I did not find. Neither Abe nor Jun Murakami has a journal record or a public expert engagement that I could find. (3) Partial or analogue results: Kakuta (arXiv 2604.10472, April 2026) proves a cone-angle deformation for the figure-eight knot below alpha_0 approx 1.7648, which includes the standard figure-eight case at alpha = 0 and is partly computer-assisted; H. Murakami (arXiv 2602.01049, Feb 2026) gives two-regime asymptotics for the figure-eight at complex parameters; Hughes et al. (arXiv 2502.18575, Feb 2025) give neural-network evidence and propose a modified phase and an improved (conjectural) statement, and prove nothing. (4) Andersen-Kashaev / Teichmuller TQFT form (a distinct formulation that I record as a neighbour, since the abstract calls it its own conjecture): Ben Aribi-Gueritaud-Piguet-Nakazawa (2019, refereed in Quantum Topology) for all twist knots; Ben Aribi-Wong (arXiv 2410.10776, Oct 2024) for every hyperbolic twist knot and FAMED-triangulated knots among the first 42,000 hyperbolic knots; Ben Aribi-Guilloux-Wong (arXiv 2512.17437, Dec 2025) for more than 42,000 knots by computer search (Regina and SnapPy). (5) Older proven cases are recorded as events (torus knots 1999; figure-eight by Ekholm, year only; Borromean rings 2005, a link; Whitehead doubles 2005; zero-volume knots and links 2008; cables of figure-eight 2009). (6) Neighbours that answer different questions, recorded so the later pass can see them: Chen-Yang Turaev-Viro 3-manifold results (Detcherry-Kalfagianni-Yang 2017; Ge-Meng-Wang-Yang 2024; Detcherry-Kalfagianni-Marasinghe 2025; Ce Shen 2026); quantum modularity (Aistleitner-Hauke 2025; Putrov-Singh 2025); and the 1-loop/torsion result (Garoufalidis-Yoon 2024). The AI question. In the sources I opened, no AI system is credited with the mathematics of the volume conjecture, and the only AI-related items are: (a) Hughes et al.'s feedforward neural network, which is the authors' own unnamed ML model; I record it in ai.systems as a close call, because it produced the predictive result that motivated the modified phase but not any theorem; (b) an acknowledgement in Ce Shen's 2609.11839 (Sept 2026), which a search result quoted as 'The results were obtained with assistance from GPT-6 Astra'. I could not verify that wording: the PDF is binary to my fetcher, the HTML text ends before the acknowledgements, and papers.cool omits them. So the attribution rests on an unverified quote, and the paper is about the Chen-Yang Turaev-Viro conjecture for shadow-link fillings, not the knot statement. Searches for AI and the volume conjecture in OpenAI, DeepMind, Anthropic (Claude), Gemini, AlphaEvolve and Lean turned up nothing on this conjecture. The DeepMind 2021 knot work concerns the signature and hyperbolic invariants, a different conjecture. The OpenAI July 2026 Cycle Double Cover claim and the August 2026 'Astra' ten-problems announcement concern other problems, as far as the snippets show. Computer-assisted work (FAMED searches, Kakuta's numerical threshold, Murakami's numerical checks) is not AI. Close calls: (i) whether the Andersen-Kashaev / Teichmuller form is the same problem as the Kashaev / colored-Jones form (the Wikipedia wording admits either reading; I did not settle it); (ii) whether a family result (twist knots, double twist knots) moves a statement quantified over all knots; (iii) whether Borromean rings, a link, falls under a knot statement; (iv) whether Hughes et al.'s modified phase is a result on this problem or a changed version (I read it as a changed version); (v) whether an unnamed trained network counts as an AI system (recorded, not decided).
competing_reading: The twist-knot and double-twist-knot claims (Abe 2020 with revisions to 2024; Jun Murakami 2024-25; the Chen-Zhu 2025 talk) are, if right, proofs of the classical Kashaev-Murakami-Murakami form for infinite families of hyperbolic knots, with the family covering all twist knots and all double twist knots. On that reading the problem has moved substantially in the window, because the statement is about all knots and each family is a large, structured part of the knot population. The strongest case against counting these as resolutions of the problem is that none is refereed in public, that Abe's claim has 19 versions and no journal record, that Jun Murakami records a gap in Lemma B that has been repaired without outside check, and that the talk claim has no written proof I could find. Read alone, the family claims are candidate events; read against the Kashaev statement, they settle only parts of it.
what_would_settle_it: (1) A referee report, journal acceptance or an expert write-up of Abe (arXiv 2012.05441, latest version) and of Jun Murakami (arXiv 2501.00225 v3), with the form of the limit stated. (2) The Chen-Zhu full text, including whether the 2025 revision (v2 of 2307.12963) asserts the volume limit for twist knots. (3) The Shen preprint's acknowledgements read directly from the TeX source or PDF, with the author's account of what the model did; if the quote is confirmed, the question is whether the assistance produced load-bearing mathematics. (4) A published statement on whether the Andersen-Kashaev / Teichmuller TQFT form and the Kashaev / colored Jones form are equivalent for twist knots; this decides whether the 2019 and 2024 results bear on the same statement. (5) A journal record for Kakuta (2604.10472) and Hughes et al. (2502.18575).

event.what_happened: Jun Murakami, 'Complexified tetrahedrons, fundamental groups, and volume conjecture for double twist knots' (arXiv 2501.00225). v1 31 Dec 2024; v2 4 Mar 2025 (per the fetch); v3 2 May 2025, with comment 'add Appendix E, fix the gap of Lemma B'. Abstract: proves the volume conjecture for double twist knots, using complexified tetrahedra and an SL(2,C) representation of the fundamental group; colored Jones polynomial written via a quantum 6j symbol. Talks in 2024 (Tokyo seminar listing, Kyoto slides) preceded the arXiv posting; the write-up date is used here.
event.revisions: v1 31 Dec 2024; v2 4 Mar 2025; v3 2 May 2025 (adds Appendix E, fixes a gap in Lemma B).
event.delivers: Claims the volume conjecture for all double twist knots. The abstract does not say which form (colored Jones at e^{2 pi i/N} or complexified SL(2,C)) is proved. The 2024 slides state the target as 2 pi lim log|V_{N-1}(K)|/N = Vol + i CS, the complexified form. A seminar abstract says the ADO invariant is used in place of colored Jones. Both points need checking.
event.remains: Whether the claim is the Kashaev/colored Jones form; all knots outside double twist knots.
event.doubts: (1) The author himself records a gap in Lemma B, repaired in v3; the repair is not independently checked. (2) The seminar abstract says the ADO invariant replaces colored Jones, which would change the object. (3) Target statement is the complexified form, so the real part needs checking against the Wikipedia form. (4) No journal publication found. (5) No external engagement found in searches; these are not exhaustive. (6) Double twist knots include twist knots, so this overlaps the Abe claim.
event.direction: Claims the conjecture for an infinite family of hyperbolic knots, in a complexified SL(2,C) form that may differ from the colored Jones form.

judgement.why: The statement is the knot volume conjecture (Kashaev/Murakami-Murakami), quantified over all knots, so proofs for knot families (torus, figure-eight, Whitehead doubles, zero-volume, cables, twist and double twist knots) are cases. Results for links (Borromean rings, Whitehead chains, multi-piece links), for distinct named conjectures (Andersen-Kashaev/Teichmuller TQFT, Chen-Yang Turaev-Viro for 3-manifolds, quantum modularity), for cone-angle or complex-parameter deformations, and Hughes et al.'s modified phase are variants. Asymptotic-expansion refinements without the volume limit (Chen-Zhu 2023, Garoufalidis-Yoon) are none. Abe's 2020 claim stays dated 2020 because the record shows no new mathematics in the 2024 revision. Among post-snapshot events, only Jun Murakami (double twist knots) and the Chen-Zhu talk claim are cases; both are unreviewed and doubtful but kept. On AI: Hughes et al.'s network made predictions that motivated a changed conjecture and is part of no proof, so none. Ce Shen's quoted acknowledgement is unverified and vague ('obtained with assistance') and does not say what the model produced, so none (F12). The event is a variant either way.
judgement.doubts: Two close calls. (1) Whether the loose wording 'quantum invariants' takes in the Andersen-Kashaev form. If it does, Ben Aribi-Wong 2024 would be a case (every hyperbolic twist knot). I read that form as a separately named conjecture. (2) Jun Murakami's claim may be about the complexified or ADO-invariant form, not the colored Jones limit; if so it would be a variant. The Chen-Zhu 'talk' event rests on an unopened seminar listing. If Shen's GPT-6 Astra acknowledgement is confirmed and specifies load-bearing work, that event's ai_role could be assisted; the event is still a variant, so the status would not change.
